title: Custom Field Self-Service for Jira
body:
For Jira admins and project admins. Find out what Custom Field Self-Service for Jira does, who it is for and where to start.

Custom Field Self-Service for Jira, by SUPERPORT.

In most Jira sites, only Jira admins can change custom fields. Every new dropdown option becomes a ticket, and fields nobody uses pile up. Custom Field Self-Service for Jira lets project admins look after the fields of their own space themselves: add and tidy up dropdown options, request new fields and see which fields are really used. Every change is checked against the guidelines your Jira admins set. Changes that affect other spaces go to a Jira admin for approval, with a before/after picture. Every change is logged and can be undone.

How it works

From setup to everyday use in four steps.

What you can do

📋 See every field of your space

The Fields tab of a space.

One list with every field your space uses, its type, who shares it and how many options it has. You see at once what you can change yourself.

✏️ Change options safely

The options editor with usage and a rename warning.

Add, rename, sort and disable options. Before you save, you see how many work items are affected. Options are never deleted, so existing work items keep their value.

🩺 Keep fields healthy

Clean-up suggestions on the Field health tab.

Find fields that are unused, on no screen or look like duplicates, with clean-up suggestions built from your own data.

Also included: approvals in your Jira Service Management space with one-click decisions, a two-person rule for large changes, an audit log with Undo, a daily self-test and a site check with one-click fixes, and the optional Field Assistant, a Rovo agent that prepares requests in a conversation (off until a Jira admin turns it on).

Who it is for

 #FFF4EE :busts_in_silhouette:

Project admins

  • See every field your space uses.
  • Maintain the options of fields only your space uses (directly or with approval, as your Jira admins decide).
  • Request new fields and changes to shared fields.
  • Decide on field requests from your team.
  • See the field health of your space.

Start with the User guide.

 #EAF2FF :shield:

Jira admins

  • Set the guidelines, approvers and the spaces where the app runs.
  • Approve or reject requests in one click.
  • Change any field directly – logged and undoable.
  • See the health of every custom field on the site.
  • Turn safe mode and the AI features on or off.

Start with Getting started.

Explore the documentation

title: Custom Field Self-Service – Getting started
body:
For Jira admins. You will install Custom Field Self-Service for Jira, learn what Jira asks you to approve and why, and set the app up so your project admins can start. Plan about 15 minutes.

 2

Before you start

You need:

  • Jira admin rights on your Jira Cloud site. Only Jira admins can install and set up the app.
  • At least one company-managed space for the project admins. Team-managed spaces are not supported: their fields belong to the space itself.
  • An approval space where the app raises approval requests. A Jira Service Management space works best, because approvals then land in your usual service queue.
  • One or more approvers who are Jira admins. Plan a backup approver too, so requests are decided when someone is away.

Start with one or two pilot spaces. You can add more spaces at any time.

Install the app

  1. Open the Custom Field Self-Service for Jira listing on the Atlassian Marketplace. You can also search for "Custom Field Self-Service" in Jira under Settings (⚙️) → Apps → Explore apps.
  2. Select Try it free and choose your site.
  3. Review the permissions Jira shows (explained below) and confirm the installation.
  4. Wait for Jira to confirm that the app is installed.

The app is paid via Atlassian and free for up to 10 users. Atlassian handles the trial, licence and billing.

What Jira asks you to approve, and why

During installation Jira lists the permissions (scopes) the app needs. In plain words:

Jira says the app can…Why the app needs it
Read Jira work (read:jira-work)Read custom fields, their contexts, options and screens, and count work items with a value, to show fields, usage and the impact of a change.
Write Jira work (write:jira-work)Create and comment approval requests; copy values when a text field is turned into a dropdown.
Read user information (read:jira-user)Show people's names and check a person's permissions in a space.
Manage Jira configuration (manage:jira-configuration)Create fields, contexts and options, change options and defaults, and put fields on screens – only after the guideline check or an approval.
Manage projects (manage:jira-project)Read a space's screen schemes, to find the screens only that space uses.
Read and write service requests, read and write request types (Jira Service Management)Raise approval requests in your approval space, record decisions, and create a hidden request type for them if the space has none.
App storage (storage:app)Keep settings, the audit log, approval records, undo snapshots and short-lived caches.

The app runs on Atlassian (Forge) and calls nothing outside Atlassian. Details: Security & privacy.

Where to find the app in Jira

WhoWhereWhat it is
Jira adminsSettings (⚙️) → Apps → Custom Field Self-Service for JiraThe Control centre: approvals, audit log, configuration and health checks.
Project admins and Jira adminsIn a space: Space settings → Custom Field Self-Service for JiraThe project page: fields, requests, audit log and field health of that space.
Everyone in an enabled spaceA work item → ••• → Request a custom fieldAsk for a missing field through the Field Assistant (only when the AI features are on).
Everyone with RovoRovo chat → agent Field AssistantPrepare requests in a conversation (only when the AI features are on).

Set it up in five steps

A new installation is switched off in every space until you set it up. Open the control centre (Settings → Apps → Custom Field Self-Service for Jira). The card Finish the setup lists what is left; each step turns to GreenDone when it is complete. A short tour explains the page the first time you open it.

Step 1: Choose the spaces where the app runs

  1. Open the Configuration tab.
  2. Under Spaces where it runs, pick your pilot spaces.

Shortcut: as a Jira admin, open the app in a space (Space settings → Custom Field Self-Service for Jira) and select Enable for <space key>. On a fresh installation, the first Jira admin who does this also becomes the first approver.

Step 2: Pick the approval space

  1. On the Configuration tab, go to Approval requests.
  2. Choose the Approval space, then the Work type. The list shows which work types have an approval step.
  3. In a Jira Service Management space, choose a Request type. If there is none that fits, select Create hidden request type "Custom field change". It is hidden from the portal; only the app raises it.
  4. Check the status next to the approval setup: GreenReady means everything fits. YellowWorks, with notes or RedNeeds a fix list what to change.

Step 3: Add approvers

  1. Under Approvers, add the Jira admins who decide requests.
  2. Under Backup approvers (added on escalation), add at least one more person.
  3. Select Save settings at the top or bottom of the page. New settings apply within 30 seconds.

Step 4: Create the self-test field

The app tests itself every day on a field of its own in the approval space. In the Finish the setup card, select Create self-test field.

Step 5: Run the site check

  1. Open the Health tab and find Site compatibility.
  2. Select Run site check. It can take up to a minute.
  3. If fixes are offered, select Fix all, or apply them one by one.

Then decide how much project admins may do

On the Configuration tab, under Option changes by project admins, choose one:

  • Approval by a Jira administrator (default) – every change a project admin makes becomes a request.
  • Directly, for fields only their space uses – project admins change these options right away. Every change is still logged, and the guard rails still apply.

Shared and global fields always need a Jira admin. Save, then tell your project admins where to find the app.

What your project admins see: the app's page in Space settings, with every field of the space.

You're done when…

#E9F7EF :white_check_mark:
  • The Finish the setup card is gone from the control centre (all steps are done).
  • The approval setup shows Ready and Site compatibility shows Compatible.
  • You open a pilot space, select View as project admin and see the fields the way your project admins will.
  • A test request from a project admin shows up on the Approvals tab, and you can approve it.

Next: the Admin guide explains every setting.

Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Custom Field Self-Service – User guide
body:
For project admins (and anyone who wants a new field). You will learn how to find your fields, change dropdown options, request new fields, decide your team's requests, undo a change and tidy up unused fields.

 2

Open the app in your space

  1. Go to your space and open Space settings.
  2. Select Custom Field Self-Service for Jira.
  3. The first time, a short tour shows you around. Select Tour in the header to see it again.

The page has these tabs: Fields, My requests, Requests for you, Audit log and Field health. Above the tabs you find the language switch (EN / DE), the live dot, the Tour button and Request field.

A line above the list tells you what happens to your changes, for example:

  • "You are a project admin: your changes are sent to a Jira administrator for approval."
  • "You are a project admin: you change the options of fields only this space uses directly; everything else goes to a Jira administrator for approval."

Which one you see depends on how your Jira admin set up the app.

The live dot means the page updates by itself when something changes – also when someone else changes a field. It also refreshes every minute.

Find a field and see what you can change

The Fields tab: every field of the space with its type, context and options.

  1. Open the Fields tab.
  2. Type part of the name or the field ID (for example customfield_10119) into Search name or ID.
  3. Narrow the list with the filters:
    • All – every field your space uses.
    • Editable – fields with options you can change or request changes for.
    • Only this space – the field's context (its set of options) belongs to your space alone.
    • Multiple – several spaces share the context and its options.
    • Global and System – the same everywhere; read-only here.
  4. Look at the button at the end of each row:
    • Edit options – you change the options directly.
    • Request change – you can prepare a change; a Jira admin approves it.
    • Details – you can look, but not change anything.
    • Read only – a system field, managed in Jira itself.
  5. Select a row to open the field. You see its description, how many work items have a value, when it was last used, Where it is used (the context marked Used here is the one your space uses) and its Screens.

Only this space · global for other spaces means your space has its own context, while all other spaces share a global one. You can maintain your own context's options.

Change the options of a dropdown field

The options editor: usage per option, the default, a rename warning and the "Add new options" panel.

  1. On the Fields tab, open a field with Edit options or Request change.
  2. Scroll to Options. The Uses column shows how many work items have each option.
  3. Make your changes:
    • Add: under Add new options, choose One at a time (type a name, press Enter) or Several at once (paste one option per line, for example from Excel). Duplicates are skipped. New options go to the end.
    • Copy from another field: select Copy from field…, choose a field of your space and select Use these options. Nothing changes in the other field.
    • Rename: type the new name into the option's box.
    • Reorder: drag the handle ⋮⋮, or select Sort A–Z, Sort Z–A or Most used first. Tick Disabled options last when sorting to keep retired options at the bottom.
    • Retire: clear Enabled next to an option. Disable unused retires every option no work item uses.
    • Default: select the circle in the Default column. A field has at most one default.
  4. Check the panels on the right before you save:
    • Impact on existing work items – how many work items a rename or a disabled option affects.
    • Impact radar – saved filters and automation rules that use this field.
    • Two-person rule – shown when the change touches many work items; then a second person approves it.
  5. Select Save changes (if you may change the field directly) or Send for approval. Discard throws your changes away.

Renaming an option changes the value in every work item that uses it. JQL filters, automations and dashboards that use the old name may stop working. Check the Impact radar first.

Options are never deleted, only disabled. Existing work items keep their value, but nobody can choose the option any more. This keeps your history and reports intact.

If the field shows "… changes this field and is waiting for approval", another request for the same field is still open. You can make new changes once it has been decided.

Request a new field

  1. Select Request field in the header. The page Request a new field opens with three steps.
  2. 1 Field: enter the Name, a Description and the Field type. For dropdown-type fields, add the Options (One at a time or Several at once) and, if you like, one Default value. Explain What is the field needed for?
  3. 2 Context: your space is always included. Add other Spaces by key or name if they need the same field (your Jira admin sets the maximum; 10 by default). Choose All issue types or Only selected.
  4. 3 Screens: tick the screens the field should appear on. Only screens your space uses alone can be picked; shared screens show a lock.
  5. Watch the summary card Your request on the right. The guideline check runs while you type:
    • GreenFits the guidelines
    • YellowFits, with notes for the approver
    • RedFix the points below – for example a reserved name, a name that is too short, or too many options.
  6. Select Send request. You see Request sent with a link to the approval request. Select Open My requests to follow it.
  • If a similar field already exists, the app says so and offers Use this field. Reusing keeps reports consistent and avoids duplicates.
  • If your Jira admin keeps a catalogue of standard fields, a matching request is pre-approved.
  • Your draft is saved automatically. Next time you are asked Continue your draft "…"?
  • If you add other spaces, their project admins are told that the field is still missing on their screens and can add it with one click.
  • With several spaces, the context no longer belongs to your space alone: its options are then maintained by a Jira admin.

Follow your requests

  1. Open My requests. Open requests are at the top, closed ones under Closed.
  2. Each request shows its status: YellowWaiting for approval GreenDone RedFail RedRejected GreyWithdrawn. A rejected request shows the approver's reason.
  3. To take back an open request, select Withdraw request. Nothing is changed.

Open requests can't be edited. To change one, withdraw it and send a new request.

Decide requests from your team

People in your space who are not project admins can ask for fields too. Their requests come to the project admins first.

  1. Open Requests for you. The number on the tab shows how many wait for you.
  2. Select a request. Under What changes once you approve you see a before/after picture.
  3. Select Approve, or write a Comment to the requester and select Reject. A rejection always needs a reason.
  4. To decide several at once, tick them and use Approve or Reject in the selection bar.

Requests marked Stage 1: project admins decide go on to a Jira admin for the final approval when needed. Nobody can approve their own request.

Add a new field to your screens

When a new field was approved for your space together with another space, it appears under New fields for your screens with Not on your screens yet. Tick your screens and select Add to my screens, or select Not needed here.

See who changed what, and undo a change

  1. Open the Audit log tab. At the top you see the time saved for your Jira admins and how many changes were made directly, approved or are waiting.
  2. Filter by Period, Field, Status or Person.
  3. To undo one of your changes, select Request undo on its row. As a project admin, your undo goes to a Jira admin for approval, like any other change.

Right after a change, the notification at the bottom of the page also offers Undo or Request undo.

Undo puts back what was there before. Options the change added are retired, not deleted. Entries in the audit log can't be changed. If there was a later change on the same field, undo that one first.

Tidy up unused fields

Field health: clean-up suggestions with "Show them".

  1. Open Field health. You see only the fields your space uses, counted in your space.
  2. Read the Suggestions, for example fields that hold values but are on none of your screens, or fields that look like duplicates.
  3. Select Show them to list the fields behind a suggestion. Select a field to open it.
  4. Below, the Findings table shows each field with With a value and Last used. Filter it by finding.

Unused means no work item in your space has a value, or Jira last saw a value 180 or more days ago. Last used is when a work item with a value in this field was last updated.

The app also scans the latest work items every night. It may suggest that a text field should probably be a dropdown, or that people type something like "Channel: …" by hand. A Jira admin can turn these into fields.

Removing fields from screens or deleting them is done by a Jira admin. Use the suggestions to start that conversation.

Ask the Field Assistant (if your site uses it)

The Field Assistant is a Rovo agent. It is off until a Jira admin turns on the AI features. When it is on, you see Ask Field Assistant in the header.

  1. Select Ask Field Assistant, or open Rovo chat and choose Field Assistant.
  2. Describe what you need in plain words, for example: "Add an option Critical to Review Priority."
  3. The assistant checks for existing fields, runs the guideline check and shows a preview with the impact.
  4. Confirm the preview. Only then does the change run or become a request – with the same rights you have on the page.

A preview is valid for 15 minutes. If it expired, ask the assistant to preview it again. Changes made through the assistant are marked via Rovo in the audit log.

AI results can be wrong. Always read the preview before you confirm.

Ask for a field from a work item (everyone)

When the AI features are on, anyone in an enabled space can ask for a missing field:

  1. Open a work item and select ••• → Request a custom field.
  2. Describe under Which field is missing on …? what people should be able to record and the choices, if any.
  3. Select Ask Field Assistant. The assistant opens in the Rovo panel with your request.
  4. Confirm the preview. If you are not a project admin, the request goes to the space's project admins, and you get an e-mail when they decide.

When the AI features are off, the dialog says Field Assistant is turned off. Project admins can then use Open Custom fields to go to the app's page; everyone else asks a project admin.

Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Custom Field Self-Service – Admin guide
body:
For Jira admins. You will learn how to decide requests, what every setting in the control centre does, how the guard rails and the AI switch work, and how to keep an eye on the app's health. For the first setup, see Getting started.

 2

Roles and permissions

The app checks every person's role with Jira on the server, for every action. Hiding a button in the browser is only for clarity, never for security.

RoleCan
Jira adminConfigure the app in the control centre, see the health of every custom field on the site, change fields directly (logged and undoable), approve requests.
Project adminSee the fields their space uses; change options of fields only their space uses (directly or with approval, as you decide); request new fields and other changes; decide requests from their team (first stage); undo their own changes as a request. Field health shows only their space.
Everyone elseAsk for a field from a work item through the Field Assistant (when the AI features are on). The space's project admins decide first.

Nobody can approve their own request. Only Jira admins give the final approval. Someone who approved the first stage of a request can't also give the final approval.

Open the control centre

Go to Settings (⚙️) → Apps → Custom Field Self-Service for Jira. The control centre has four tabs: Approvals, Audit log, Configuration and Health. Select Tour for a one-minute walk-through.

Banners at the top warn you about things to fix, for example Test settings are on: switch them off before real use, or that there is only one approver. When safe mode is on, the header shows RedSafe mode on.

Decide requests

  1. Open the Approvals tab. The number on the tab shows how many requests wait.
  2. Select a request in Open requests. The details show who asked and why, why it needs approval, the risk, and what the app will do after approval.
  3. Choose:
    • Approve (or Approve and create for a new field) – the app carries out exactly the change shown.
    • Reject – write a Comment to the requester first; a reason of at least 3 characters is required.
    • Cancel request – withdraws a request that should not be decided.
  4. To clear the queue quickly, select Approve all low-risk (n).

Your decision goes through Jira's approval as you, so Jira checks that you are an approver. The app then checks again who approved, carries the change out, logs it and tells the requester. Approvers get an e-mail per request and, if switched on, a daily digest. You can also decide on the project page under Requests for you.

Work with fields as a Jira admin

The project page as a Jira admin: "Add field", "View as project admin" and direct changes.

On a space's page (Space settings → Custom Field Self-Service for Jira) you work directly:

  • Add field creates a field at once when you confirm. You can also give it a Global context.
  • Open a field to Edit its name and description, Change spaces of its context, Manage its screens, or Take out of use… (removes it from every screen; values stay, Undo puts it back).
  • View as project admin shows the page exactly as the space's project admins see it, with changes switched off. Select Back to my view to return.
  • On Field health you see every changeable custom field of the site. Tick fields to Put on this space's screens or Take out of use, use Create dropdown on a text field that should be a dropdown (copying the existing values), and Check for outside changes to find options changed outside the app.

Every change is logged. A notification offers Undo right away, and the audit log keeps it available.

Configuration

All settings are on the Configuration tab. Nothing applies until you select Save settings; the app, the Field Assistant and the guideline check then use the new settings within 30 seconds. Discard throws unsaved changes away.

Option changes by project admins

ChoiceEffect
Approval by a Jira administrator (default)Every change a project admin makes becomes a request.
Directly, for fields only their space usesProject admins change these options right away. Logged; the guard rails still apply.

Shared and global fields always need a Jira admin.

Spaces per context

Maximum – how many spaces a project admin may pick when requesting a new field. Default: 10, the own space included.

Approval requests

  • Approval space, Work type and (in Jira Service Management) Request type – where the app raises its approval requests. Create hidden request type "Custom field change" creates one that only the app uses. The status shows Ready, Works, with notes or Needs a fix; Check again re-checks.
  • Approvers – Jira admins who decide requests.
  • Backup approvers (added on escalation).
  • Remind approvers after (hours) – default 24. Escalate after (hours) – default 48. Stage 1 escalates to the approvers, stage 2 to the backups.
  • Allow self-approvals – leave it off (No · production). Turn it on only for testing.
  • E-mail the requester when a request is approved, rejected or executed.
  • Raise an alert work item when something fails – select How it looks for a preview.
  • Daily digest e-mail to approvers with what is waiting – the preview can also Send this e-mail to me.

If the approval space is not a Jira Service Management space, request types don't exist there and the app runs the approval itself.

Allowed field types

The types project admins can request. By default: Select list (single), Select list (multiple), Checkboxes, Radio buttons, Text (single line), Paragraph, Number and Date. You can also allow Date and time, User picker (single) and Labels. New cascading select fields are not offered.

Audit log retention

Delete entries after: Keep forever (default), 12, 24 or 36 months. Older entries are deleted every night.

New fields on screens

  • At the bottom of the first tab (default) – always the same place.
  • Next to the most similar field – the app puts the new field right after the most alike field on that screen.

Spaces where it runs

Everywhere else, the page, the agent and the work item action only say "not enabled". None picked means all spaces – but only after the settings were saved once.

AI features

AI features (Rovo agent) is Greyoff by default. When you turn it on and save, the Field Assistant can be used in Rovo and the AI buttons appear in the app. When it is off, the Field Assistant and all AI buttons are hidden, and the work item action Request a custom field explains that the assistant is turned off.

  • The assistant works within each person's own Jira permissions and previews every change before the person confirms it.
  • Only Jira admins can change this switch. Every change is logged in the audit log.
  • If SUPERPORT has to stop the AI features for a while, you see "Temporarily turned off by the app vendor." Your setting is kept and applies again afterwards.

AI results can be wrong and must be reviewed. Rovo conversations are processed by Atlassian Rovo under Atlassian's terms and settings.

Guard rails

  • Safe mode – every change becomes an approval request; nothing runs directly. Safe mode also switches on by itself when the daily self-test fails or changes come in unusually fast.
  • Two-person rule from (work items) – default 100. A change touching this many work items needs approval by a second person.
  • Automatic safe mode above (changes per hour) – default 30.
  • Project admins asked per request (max.) – default 10, for requests from people who are not project admins.

Project admins also have a daily limit of direct changes; beyond it, their changes go to approval.

The fields marked TEST ONLY let you try the project admin or non-admin flow with your own account. Leave them empty in production.

Guidelines for new fields

SettingDefault
Name: min. characters / Name: max. characters3 / 40
Max. options100
Max. option length60
Similar names from0.8 (ratio 0.5–1; higher means only very similar names are flagged)
Reserved namesOne per line, in addition to Jira's system fields
Field cataloguePre-approved standard fields, one per line: Name | type | option; option | description | field ID. A matching request is green; with a field ID, the existing field is reused.
Minutes per manual ticket / Minutes per approval20 / 3 – used for the "time saved" figure in the audit log

Audit log

The control centre's Audit log tab shows every change and every request of all spaces: date, Requested by, Approved by, space, field, change and status. Filter by Period, field, status and person. Entries can't be changed. Changes made through the Field Assistant are marked via Rovo. Undo is available on the space's page.

Health checks

The Health tab shows whether the app works on your site:

  • Site compatibility – checks what differs between Jira sites. Run site check, then Fix all for what the app can set itself (for example the best work type for approvals, or switching self-approvals off).
  • Self-test – runs every day on the self-test field and on demand with Run self-test now. If it fails, safe mode switches on.
  • Background checks – the nightly checks (options changed outside the app, suggestions, the approvers' digest) and the watchdog, which looks for stuck requests every 30 minutes. Each can be started on demand.
  • Alerts – alert work items the app raised in the approval space when something failed.
  • If safe mode switched on by itself, the reason is shown here. Switch it off under Configuration → Guard rails.

Licence

The app is paid via Atlassian and free for up to 10 users. Manage the licence under Settings → Apps → Manage apps. If the licence is not active, every page and action stops with this message and changes nothing:

"The Custom Field Self-Service for Jira license of this site is not active. Nothing was changed. A Jira administrator can renew it under Jira settings > Apps > Manage apps."

Maintenance and status

If SUPERPORT has to pause the app for maintenance, users see one of two messages:

  • YellowChanges paused "Changes are paused for maintenance to keep your data safe. You can still view everything; editing will be back as soon as possible." All change buttons are disabled.
  • RedUnavailable "Custom Field Self-Service for Jira is temporarily unavailable", with View status page.

Open pages follow within a minute and come back by themselves. No data is lost. Follow the status at superapps.statuspage.io.

Data export

The app has no data export of its own. Approval requests are ordinary work items in your approval space and follow your Jira's rules.

Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Custom Field Self-Service – FAQ & troubleshooting
body:
For project admins and Jira admins. Answers to common questions, and what to do when the app shows a message you don't expect. Messages are quoted as the app shows them in English.

 2

Access and setup

I can't find the app in my space.

The app's page is in Space settings → Custom Field Self-Service for Jira. You only see Space settings if you are a project admin of that space or a Jira admin. If the page says the app is not enabled, see the next question.

 The page says "Not enabled for … yet".

The app runs only in the spaces your Jira admin picked. The message lists where it runs now.

  • Jira admins: select Enable for <space key> on that page, or add the space under Configuration → Spaces where it runs in the control centre and save.
  • Everyone else: ask your Jira admin to enable the app for your space.

A new installation is switched off everywhere until a Jira admin sets it up. See Getting started.

 I see "Project admins only".

The page is for the project admins of the space and for Jira admins. If you need a field, ask a project admin of your space – or, when the AI features are on, use ••• → Request a custom field on a work item.

 I see "Team-managed space".

The app works with company-managed spaces only. In a team-managed space, the fields belong to the space itself and are managed in the space's own settings.

 Can I use the app in German?

Yes. The app follows your Jira language. You can also switch with EN / DE in the page header; the app remembers your choice in this browser. Some messages from the server stay in English.

Fields and options

Why can't I delete an option?

Options are never deleted, only disabled. Work items that use the option keep their value, but nobody can choose it any more. This protects your history, filters and reports. Clear Enabled next to the option, or use Disable unused.

 Why does a field show "Request change" or "Details" instead of "Edit options"?

It depends on who else uses the field's options (its context):

  • Only this space – you may change the options directly, if your Jira admin allows it. Otherwise your changes go to approval.
  • Multiple, Global – other spaces would be affected, so a Jira admin decides.
  • System fields are managed in Jira itself.
 The app warns me when I rename an option. What happens?

Every work item with that option shows the new name. JQL filters, automations and dashboards that use the old name may stop working. Check the Impact radar before you save: it lists the saved filters and automation rules that use the field.

 "… changes this field and is waiting for approval."

Another request for the same field is still open. You can make new changes once it has been decided. If it is your own request and no longer needed, withdraw it under My requests.

 "The field context changed meanwhile. Reload and try again." (or "Option … no longer exists; reload and try again.")

Someone changed the field while you were editing it – in the app or in Jira. Select Refresh or reload the page, then make your change again.

 My new field is not on the screens of the other spaces I picked.

The app only puts a field on screens your own space uses alone. The project admins of the other spaces find the field under Requests for you → New fields for your screens and add it with Add to my screens. Shared screens are changed by a Jira admin in Jira itself.

 The field list or field health takes a while to load.

On large spaces the app reads the fields in several passes and shows the progress, for example "Reading the fields of this space: 40 of 120…". Counting work items can also take a moment ("Counting the work items with a value…"). The numbers update by themselves, and later visits are faster because the app keeps a short-lived cache.

 Field health says a field is "Unused", but I know it has values.

Unused means no work item (in your space, for project admins) has a value, or a work item with a value was last updated 180 or more days ago. Jira does not record when a field value itself changed, so Last used is the date such a work item was last updated. The counts are refreshed every few hours.

Requests and approvals

How long does an approval take?

That depends on your approvers. The app reminds them after 24 hours and escalates to the backup approvers after 48 hours (your Jira admin can change both). You can follow every request under My requests, and you get an e-mail when it is decided if your Jira admin switched that on.

 "Give a reason for the rejection: the requester sees it."

A rejection always needs a comment of at least 3 characters. Write it in Comment to the requester, then select Reject again.

 "You asked for this change, so someone else has to decide (self-approvals are off)."

Nobody approves their own request. Ask another approver to decide. Related messages: "You approved the first stage, so someone else gives the final approval." and "Only Jira administrators give the final approval."

 Why did my change go to approval although I can usually change this field directly?

One of the guard rails applied. The reason is shown with the request, for example:

  • "Two-person rule: the change touches … work items (threshold …)." – large changes need a second person.
  • "Daily limit reached: … of … direct changes today." – more changes today go to approval.
  • The banner Safe mode is on – every change goes to a Jira admin until safe mode is switched off. It can switch on by itself when the daily self-test fails or changes come in unusually fast.

Undo and audit log

How do I undo a change?

Open the Audit log tab on the space's page and select Undo (Jira admins) or Request undo (project admins, approved by a Jira admin) on the entry. Right after a change, the notification also offers it. Options the change added are retired, not deleted.

 "A later change on the same field came after this one. Undo the later change first, so nothing else is lost."

Undo the newest change on that field first, then the older one. Related messages: "This change was already undone." and "An undo of this change is already waiting for approval."

Field Assistant (AI)

"Field Assistant is turned off" when I use "Request a custom field".

The AI features are off by default. A Jira admin can turn them on in the control centre: Configuration → AI features → AI features (Rovo agent) → Save settings. Until then, project admins use the app's page (Open Custom fields); everyone else asks a project admin. If the message says the features are "temporarily turned off by the app vendor", try again later.

 The Field Assistant says my preview has expired.

A preview is valid for 15 minutes and can be used once. Ask the assistant to preview the change again, then confirm.

Licence and availability

"The Custom Field Self-Service for Jira license of this site is not active."

The trial has ended or the licence was not renewed. Nothing was changed. A Jira admin can renew it under Settings → Apps → Manage apps.

 "Changes are paused for maintenance" or "temporarily unavailable".

SUPERPORT has paused the app for maintenance to keep your data safe. Nothing you saved is lost. While changes are paused you can still view everything. The page comes back by itself; follow the progress on the status page.

 A change showed an error instead of a success message.

Atlassian limits how much any Forge app may do in a short time. If a limit is reached during a change, the app shows an error. The audit log shows what was applied, and undo stays available. Try the rest again a little later. If it keeps failing, contact support.

Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Custom Field Self-Service – Security & privacy
body:
For Jira admins, security and privacy teams. You will learn where the app runs, what it stores and for how long, which permissions it needs and why, how personal data and AI are handled, and what happens when you uninstall.

 2

At a glance

#E9F7EF :lock:
  • BlueRuns on Atlassian The app runs entirely on Atlassian's cloud platform (Forge). Its functions, storage and pages are hosted by Atlassian.
  • No data leaves Atlassian. The app calls only Jira and Jira Service Management through Forge. It sends nothing to SUPERPORT or anyone else. SUPERPORT has no access to your Jira site, your work items or the data the app stores.
  • Data residency: app data is kept in Forge storage and follows your site's Atlassian data residency.
  • No logins of its own: the app uses your Jira sign-in only. It has no passwords or tokens of its own.
  • Personal data: only Atlassian account IDs. Names and e-mail addresses are not stored; names are looked up from Jira when shown.
  • AI: off by default. Only a Jira admin can turn it on.

Permissions (scopes) and why the app needs them

ScopeUsed for
read:jira-workRead custom fields, contexts, options, screens and work item counts, to show fields, usage and impact.
write:jira-workCreate and comment approval requests; copy values when a text field is converted to a dropdown.
read:jira-userShow people's names; check a user's permissions in a space.
manage:jira-configurationCreate custom fields, contexts and options, change options and defaults, put fields on screens – after the guideline check or an approval.
manage:jira-projectRead a space's screen schemes, to find the screens only that space uses.
read:servicedesk-request, write:servicedesk-requestRaise approval requests in the approval space you chose; read and record approvals.
read:requesttype:jira-service-management, write:requesttype:jira-service-managementFind the approval request type, and create a hidden one if the approval space has none.
storage:appSettings, audit log, approval records, undo snapshots, caches.

Who can do what

Every role check runs on the server against Jira, for every call. The browser never decides who may do what.

  • Jira admins configure the app, see the health of every field on the site, change fields directly (logged and undoable) and approve requests.
  • Project admins see only the fields of their space and nothing about other spaces' fields or work items. They request changes, or change options of fields only their space uses directly if a Jira admin allows it.
  • Other users can ask for a field from a work item; the project admins decide first.

Guard rails on every change: the guideline check, safe mode, a daily limit of direct changes per person, a two-person rule for changes touching many work items, a check that the approver is allowed and is not the requester, and a lock against parallel changes to the same field. Every executed change is written to the audit log with the person, time, old and new value.

What the app stores, and for how long

DataContainsKept
SettingsApproval space, approvers (account IDs), guideline rules, field catalogueUntil changed
Audit logWho, when, which field, old and new value, approver, request keyAs long as the Jira admin's retention setting says (default: kept); older entries are deleted nightly
Approval recordsThe requested change, requester and approvers, decisionWith the audit log
Undo snapshotsThe options of a field before a changeAs long as needed for undo
Drafts and previewsA person's unsent form; Field Assistant previewsDrafts 7 days; previews 15 minutes
Usage countsPer field: how many work items have a value, and when such a work item was last updated – no work item contentRecounted every 6 hours
Nightly suggestionsShort repeated text values and up to three work item keys from the latest 100 work items of a spaceReplaced every night
Per-person conveniencesWhether the tour was seen, the last visit, a daily change counterUntil the person's account is closed or the app is uninstalled
CachesField overview, option catalogue, usage suggestionsMinutes to a day, refreshed automatically

Approval requests are created as Jira work items in the approval space you choose. They are your Jira data and follow your Jira's rules.

Personal data and people who leave

The app stores only Atlassian account IDs of people who request, approve, change or undo something. Once a week it reports these account IDs to Atlassian's personal data reporting service. For every account Atlassian reports as closed, the app replaces the account ID with "closed-account" in the audit log and approval records, and deletes the records about that person alone (drafts, tour, last visit, daily counter).

AI features (Field Assistant)

  • The Field Assistant is an Atlassian Rovo agent. Conversations are processed by Atlassian Rovo under Atlassian's terms and settings.
  • The AI features are off by default. Only a Jira admin can turn them on (control centre → Configuration → AI features), and every switch is logged.
  • The assistant acts only through the app's own actions, with the permissions of the person using it. It previews every change; nothing runs before the person confirms.
  • Changes made through the assistant are marked via Rovo in the audit log.

Sub-processors

Atlassian (hosting, storage, Rovo). SUPERPORT uses no other sub-processors for this app.

Retention and uninstalling

  • Jira admins choose which spaces use the app, who approves and how long the audit log is kept.
  • Uninstalling the app deletes its app storage according to Atlassian's Forge data retention.
  • Approval requests stay in your approval space as ordinary work items.

Availability and security response

In an emergency, SUPERPORT can pause changes (read-only) or take the app offline for all customers within about a minute, and says so on the status page. This never sends or exposes data. Customers can't change this switch, and neither can anyone reading the app's front-end code.

Please report security problems privately, not publicly: through the support portal, by e-mail to support@superport.digital, or through Atlassian's Marketplace security reporting. SUPERPORT acknowledges every report within two business days.

Legal

  • SUPERPORT EULA (covers all SUPERPORT apps, including the app privacy statement)
  • SUPERPORT privacy policy

Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Custom Field Self-Service – Release notes
body:
For Jira admins and project admins. What changed in each version of Custom Field Self-Service for Jira, newest first. Version numbers are the ones shown on the Atlassian Marketplace and under Manage apps.

3.2.0 – November 2026 GreenLatest

AI features are off by default

  • New switch AI features (Rovo agent) in the control centre under Configuration → AI features. It is off by default, also for existing installations. Only Jira admins can change it, and every change is logged in the audit log.
  • While the AI features are off, the app shows no AI buttons and the tour skips the Field Assistant. The work item action Request a custom field explains that the Field Assistant is turned off and where a Jira admin turns it on.
  • If the Field Assistant is asked while AI is off, it refuses and points to the configuration.
  • Changes made through the Field Assistant are marked via Rovo in the audit log.
  • SUPERPORT can temporarily turn the AI features off for all sites. Your setting is kept and applies again afterwards; the control centre shows "Temporarily turned off by the app vendor."

3.1.0 – November 2026 BlueFirst Marketplace release

  • Available on the Atlassian Marketplace, paid via Atlassian and free for up to 10 users. Existing installations accept the new version in Manage apps.
  • If a site's licence is not active, the app stops with a clear message and changes nothing.
  • App privacy notice; the SUPERPORT EULA covers the app.

Also in this release

Field health

  • Unused now means no work item has a value (counted per field, refreshed every few hours).
  • Last used shows when a work item with a value in the field was last updated; "not used for 180 days" uses the same date. Dates are written unambiguously.
  • Clean-up Suggestions built from the findings: values on no screen, no value and no screen, never filled in, possible duplicates and stale fields, with Show them and (for Jira admins) Select them.
  • A new With a value column. Findings are shown in the page's language.
  • Project admins see only the fields their space uses, counted in their space and checked against their space's screens. Jira admins see every changeable field of the site.

Fields

  • A space with its own context while the field also has a global one is marked Only this space · global for other spaces. The field page marks the context the space uses with Used here.

Requests and undo

  • Requests for you shows the requested change as a before/after picture.
  • Undo from the audit log and straight from the notification after a change. A project admin's undo goes to a Jira admin for approval.

Reliability and privacy

  • Maintenance messages: if SUPERPORT has to pause the app, open pages show "Changes are paused" with every change button disabled, or a "temporarily unavailable" page with a link to the status page. Both come back by themselves.
  • Personal data reporting: once a week the app reports stored account IDs to Atlassian; closed accounts are erased.

Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.
